steps.what: Plan flights using current charts, aircraft data and operational requirements
Check the proposed plan against government and company regulations and confirm suitability

tasks.design: Retain the pilot's plan construction and compliance review using the existing flight-planning application, represented by {OTHER}. Existing route and performance calculations support that work; this design claims no new saving from calculations already automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: A technically computed route still requires operational and regulatory judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital planning tools already support routes, profiles, weather restrictions and performance calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Aircraft-specific limits, changing conditions, incomplete information and operator requirements.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a technically feasible plan is suitable for the actual flight.
tasks.altitude: Planning responsibility and decision rights remain with the pilot.

reach.task: Explain a plan's operational constraints during coordination
reach.learn: Operator dispatch procedures and responsibility boundaries

evidence.claim: Lido Flight 4D supports routes, profiles, fuel planning and performance against weather and airspace restrictions; that is an existing capability rather than evidence of incremental pilot savings.

assumptions: Boundary is plan development and compliance review, excluding data gathering, route-choice judgement counted separately, external filing and aircraft operation. A roll-up must allocate overlapping plan decisions once.

OTHER means an existing approved flight-planning application. The pilot's preceding data-review process produces the reviewed input pack before s1; its gathering and checking effort belongs to task 10593, not a free new feed.

Approved data providers and the operator already maintain charts, aircraft performance data and procedures. The pilot checks applicability during the retained steps; missing or stale data require established manual planning or escalation.
Native planning configuration is the first option; no custom calculator or language model is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because this is the unchanged existing planning process, with existing application runtime excluded from labour.
unknowns: Existing planning application and operator procedures
research_questions: Which planning actions remain manual after existing approved tools, rather than merely reflecting application runtime?

already_counted.description: Plan construction and compliance review remain fully counted

incremental.description: No new process or software to maintain

approvals.approved_version: Exact checked plan version, aircraft, departure time and input-data snapshot; any change requires renewed pilot review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. Scenario assumes existing digital planning calculations and retains all incremental human planning judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check baggage or cargo position, restraint and conformity with loading requirements

tasks.design: Keep the pilot's physical loading check. A load sheet in {DOCS} can describe the intended arrangement but cannot establish that baggage and cargo are actually restrained and positioned correctly.
tasks.previous_blocker: A recorded load is not proof of its physical condition.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change replaces this physical inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden restraint defects, changed loads and discrepancies between instructions and the aircraft.
tasks.human_edge: Inspecting the actual load and requiring correction before acceptance.
tasks.altitude: The pilot's loading-check responsibility remains unchanged.

reach.task: Communicate an observed loading discrepancy clearly
reach.learn: Aircraft loading limits and restraint requirements

evidence.claim: Physical loading verification remains distinct from producing a digital weight-and-balance calculation.

assumptions: Boundary is the pilot's inspection, excluding loading crew execution, load-sheet calculation and correction work by handlers.

The loading crew produces the actual loaded state before the inspection and the operator's existing loading process supplies instructions. No structured loading-complete flag or discrepancy code is assumed to prove safety.
The pilot produces any discrepancy through this fully counted inspection; correction and reinspection follow existing procedure and earn no proposed saving.
Test existing loading records before custom tools if a distinct paperwork problem is demonstrated.
Zero incremental upkeep because no change to inspection or software is proposed.
research_questions: How are late loading changes communicated and physically rechecked under current procedures?

incremental.description: No new tool or procedure to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. Digital load records do not remove the physical baggage and cargo check.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Obtain and review flight planning data

steps.what: Obtain load weights, fuel supplies, weather conditions and schedules and check their provenance
Collate checked flight data into a consistent planning review pack
Review flight data and identify needed changes before determining the flight plan

tasks.design: Configure the existing flight-planning application, represented by {OTHER}, to collate pilot-checked source records into a review pack. The pilot checks provenance, units, currency and operational meaning; incomplete or conflicting information remains visible and returns to manual preparation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate source screens and documents can require repeated collation, even though the operational review must remain.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital planning tools already handle weather, restrictions and fuel planning; a native briefing view may avoid duplicate preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising stale inputs, unit or classification errors and changes that invalidate an earlier plan.
tasks.human_edge: Connecting the data to the actual aircraft, intended flight and acceptable margins.
tasks.altitude: The pilot may spend less time assembling a pack, while the full data review and planning responsibility remain.

reach.learn: Data provenance, validity periods and operational escalation

evidence.claim: Lido Flight 4D supports planning against weather and airspace restrictions and fuel requirements; local briefing-pack integration and labour savings still need testing.
The digest describes a title-mapping error that misclassified passengers and understated take-off mass, supporting explicit input interpretation checks rather than trusting a structured load field.

assumptions: Boundary is obtaining, collating and reviewing planning inputs, not performing weight-and-balance calculations, choosing the final route, external plan filing or flying. The reviewed pack feeds the separate planning task; gathering savings are counted only here.

OTHER means an existing flight-planning and briefing application. Before s1, the loading agent produces the existing load record with flight and aircraft ID, load components, mass units and version; the fuel service record provides quantity, unit and timestamp; the weather provider supplies issue time, validity, location and briefing content; operations supplies flight ID, aircraft and scheduled times. These existing producer tasks are unchanged and receive no savings or new data-entry burden.

The pilot selects and checks sources in s1 and captures source IDs, versions, validity, units and flight/aircraft association in the selection manifest. All capture and manual interpretation time is included in the unchanged 35 percent.

The pack copies selected records without inferring passenger classes, fuel conversion assumptions or weather relevance. Missing fields or ambiguous units stop automatic collation for that record; the pilot uses manual preparation, allowed for in upkeep and the conservative range.
Test native briefing views before custom integration; if the pack is already assembled automatically, incremental saving is zero. Existing provider runtime is not labour.

Allow 8 focal hours per 100 baseline for source mappings, failed imports and sample reconciliation; allow 2 other-role hours for connector administration. Check operator approval, access and national employee consultation where relevant.
unknowns: Approved briefing configuration and required validation
research_questions: Does native pack collation save hands-on time after provenance checks, rejected inputs and source-to-pack reconciliation?

already_counted.description: Source selection, provenance checks and manifest capture remain fully counted
Operational data review and identification of changes remain fully counted

incremental.description: Maintain source mappings and resolve imports and reconciliation exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85; gross saving 15 less 8 focal upkeep gives net 7. Range 1-4 assumes manual collation remains and repeated weather or load revisions require manual reconciliation. Existing automated briefings yield zero new saving; other-role upkeep is separately visible.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Choose routes, altitudes and speeds balancing safety, conditions, comfort and operational constraints

tasks.design: Keep the pilot's route, altitude and speed choice supported by existing calculations in {OTHER}, the flight-planning application. A computed optimum remains an input to judgement about the actual flight, and no new saving is assigned to established calculations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fastest, safest and smoothest can conflict and depend on changing conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning applications already present routes and profiles for comparison.
tasks.still_hard: Weather uncertainty, traffic constraints, aircraft capability and changing operational margins.
tasks.human_edge: Making a defensible operational choice when goals and evidence conflict.
tasks.altitude: The pilot retains route-choice judgement and gains no new operational authority.

reach.task: Explain the operational reasons for a route change
reach.learn: Shared planning assumptions and operator coordination procedures

evidence.claim: Lido Flight 4D supports route and profile planning, but that capability does not demonstrate removal of pilot route-choice judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is the route-choice decision, excluding upstream data gathering, final plan compliance checking and aircraft control. A roll-up assigns any decision also described under general flight planning once.

The pilot's existing input review supplies the reviewed pack before this task; the current planning application produces route alternatives from operator-approved data. Their existing production effort and runtime are not newly saved here.
No model-selected route or structured safety flag is assumed. Missing, stale or conflicting information triggers existing manual planning or operational escalation.
Use native planning configuration before any custom tool; no change is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because this scenario retains the existing decision process and application.
unknowns: Current planning support and division of responsibilities
research_questions: Which route-choice effort is judgement, and which is already performed by existing planning calculations?

already_counted.description: Route, altitude and speed judgement remains fully counted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. Scenario already uses digital route/profile support and preserves the pilot's actual choice effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: A native briefing pack may reduce collation, while loading inspection, planning review and operational judgement remain with the pilot.
reach: Help flight operations reconcile input versions and explain planning changes
role.ambitious_version: Use dependable current inputs to support pilot decisions without treating existing calculations as newly released capacity.
